api: mxmlOptionsNew(); mxmlOptionsSetTypeValue(options, MXML_TYPE_OPAQUE); mxmlOptionsSetErrorCallback; mxmlLoadString(NULL, options, NUL-terminated copy of the local bytes); tree walk with mxmlGetType, mxmlGetFirstChild, mxmlGetNextSibling, mxmlGetParent, mxmlGetElement, mxmlElementGetAttrCount, mxmlElementGetAttrByIndex, mxmlGetOpaque, mxmlGetCDATA. Namespace resolution is done by the adapter, not by mxml
namespace_semantics: Mini-XML 4.0.6 does not implement Namespaces in XML: its documentation and sources contain no namespace handling, element and attribute names are returned as written (prefix:local) and xmlns/xmlns:p are ordinary attributes. harness.c resolves expanded names from mxml's parsed tree with an in-scope binding stack (default namespace for unprefixed elements, none for unprefixed attributes, xml prefix predefined, unbound prefix rejected).
coverage: LLVM source coverage of Mini-XML built from the pinned release (static libmxml4.a; shared library and threads disabled)
coverage_limit: Two valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE establish mxml's element, attribute, comment, processing-instruction, CDATA and character-data tree for them only. Namespace expanded names, declaration counts and URIs are computed by the adapter from mxml's qnames and xmlns attributes; mxml itself does no namespace processing. mxmlLoadString reads a NUL-terminated string, so bytes after a NUL are not parsed. DTDs, entities beyond the controls' references, other encodings, XML 1.1 and well-formedness rejection are not established. The expected outputs come from controls/xml/check_controls.py (Python pyexpat, a different family from Mini-XML); the expat and libxml2 projects give the same summaries.
